In released ssh.c, process_config_files (lines 512–540) bypasses both ordinary

candidate's -F none supplies no Include/Match source from those files.
Command switches assign no agent forwarding, no X11 and no PTY (774–776,

The config-test branch exits at 1427–1429 before provider-environment
expansion, multiplex connection, ordinary resolver and connect (1431–1475);
startup and earlier numeric/canonical processing still precede it. The
version branch exits at 834–839 but follows startup/getpwuid (599–628).
These are bounded code-path facts, not permission to run either branch.

## Literal none and forwarding cleanup

Released readconf.c applies CLEAR_ON_NONE to local/remote/proxy commands,
control path, both PKCS#11 and security-key provider fields, and the known-host
command (2547–2561); none jump-host cleanup follows (2562–2566).
This is essential for SecurityKeyProvider=none: the provider string is cleared,
rather than interpreted as a library filename. Explicit clearing follows
default filling. ClearAllForwardings selects forwarding cleanup (2368–2372).
IdentityAgent deliberately has different null/none treatment (2577), so the
candidate leaves its genuine existing selection available.
[OpenSSH 8.9p1 readconf.c](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_8_9_P1/readconf.c).

## Strict known-host acceptance and address insertion

The released known-host branch fails for a new host under strict yes
(1055–1067), and for changed/revoked keys under non-off strictness
(1143–1158, 1195–1210). A different successful-host branch can insert a
previously unknown address when CheckHostIP is true (1014–1028).
Consequently strict yes alone is insufficient for this no-write requirement.
The candidate additionally sets CheckHostIP=no; it does not replace any
host-key database or assert a verified remote exchange.
[OpenSSH 8.9p1 sshconnect.c](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_8_9_P1/sshconnect.c).

## Post-authentication host-key replacement

In update_known_hosts, a zero update_hostkeys value returns before file
metadata/replacement work (1948–1977). UpdateHostKeys=no supplies the explicit
policy guard, independent of unknown installed defaults and independent of
strict initial host checking.
[OpenSSH 8.9p1 clientloop.c](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_8_9_P1/clientloop.c).

## Authentication and its retained dependency

Released sshconnect2.c uses the preferred/supported method intersection
(2183–2218), with explicit method-enable fields (376–405). The candidate
selects publickey and disables other listed methods. Local authenticator
keys are skipped when the provider field is null (1501–1507, 1607–1612,
1630–1635). Batch handling rejects an unavailable key passphrase
(1481–1484). Agent identities remain separately obtained (1548–1574,
1644–1675), and agent signing returns through a distinct path (1159–1163).
Therefore disabling the client's local providers does not establish the
internal behavior of an existing external agent. In particular, provider
suppression is necessary beyond relying on BatchMode for security-key paths.
[OpenSSH 8.9p1 sshconnect2.c](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_8_9_P1/sshconnect2.c).

## Option-family interface coverage

The release manual defines AddKeysToAgent=no as no key addition; BatchMode
as suppressing user prompts; CanonicalizeHostname=no as no explicit rewriting;
EscapeChar=none as disabling escapes; ForkAfterAuthentication=no as no
requested backgrounding. GSSAPI authentication/delegation are distinct.
It identifies the existing IdentityAgent/SSH_AUTH_SOCK relation and the
effect of IdentitiesOnly, which the candidate does not change. It documents
negative PasswordAuthentication, KbdInteractiveAuthentication and
HostbasedAuthentication controls and the public-key method selection.
[OpenSSH 8.9p1 ssh_config.5](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_8_9_P1/ssh_config.5).

The current configuration manual is a cross-check only: ControlPath=none
disables sharing; ControlMaster=no alone would still permit using a configured
master, hence the explicit path/persistence guards. ClearAllForwardings
covers local, remote and dynamic forwards; Tunnel=no excludes tunnel-device
requests. ProxyCommand/ProxyJump none remove those routes; PermitLocalCommand
no excludes local commands. RemoteCommand is a separate configured command,
cleared here under the released source. KnownHostsCommand supplies host-key
callbacks, which are cleared. VerifyHostKeyDNS=no prevents alternative DNS
trust. PKCS11Provider none disables that provider. The documented update and
address-addition behavior supports the separate known-host guards. No
current-manual default is used as installed evidence.
[OpenSSH configuration manual](https://man.openbsd.org/ssh_config).

The client manual independently describes -F none, -a, -x, -T and the
version/config-dump interfaces. It is not evidence that a particular vendor
binary accepts these exact fields, has the same startup dependencies, or
implements the selected released branches.
[OpenSSH client manual](https://man.openbsd.org/ssh).

For capture, run/run_record_pin/previous_phase/previous_root_receipt are null.
For every successor, run and its RUN.json bytes/SHA256 pin come from the actual
accepted capture. Previous phase is the complete preceding MANIFEST.sha256
bytes/SHA256 pin; previous_root_receipt is its ROOT_RECEPTION.json reference.
These are actual prior values, never placeholders copied across phases.

Fresh protected_roles include whole Git/SSH/interpreter files and unchanged
mirror/bare config, HEAD, default-index, packed-ref and alternate roles. The
interpreter spelling's symlink/metadata/resolution is explicit. Missing roles
are actual absence states. Bare main is separately checked by real Git queries
at both endpoints and may move only in push's exact compare-and-swap. Root must
compare this fresh key to the already accepted repository roles before granting
a phase, not merely accept whatever current bytes happen to be present.

Existing HOME/USER/LOGNAME/SSH_AUTH_SOCK/SSH_AGENT_PID values, when present,
are bound as allowed inherited roles and checked unchanged. They are never
repurposed as task-specific paths. Child Git/SSH settings are constructed
explicitly as in COMMAND_RUNTIME_PROTOCOL, with the added
GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1. No credential, agent, known_hosts, config, default
index or original-mirror write is implemented. This is not a claim of hermetic
Git/SSH/ELF/configuration runtime closure or reusable scientific execution.

## Native command and product boundary

All Git invocations use explicit argv, not shell interpolation, under the
fixed bare destination and command-local hooks/fsmonitor/untracked-cache/
maintenance/gc/signing settings. Original mirror operations are restricted
to HEAD, origin and clean porcelain reads with the same safe settings.

Selected ls-tree and ls-files queries are split deterministically into sorted
batches of at most 512 exact pathnames, with each complete native return
retained. The union must be exactly the selected set. This prevents one large
argv from depending on an assumed host argument limit. The full diff-tree
query is never path-filtered or batched. No whole-baseline object-body stream
is read; cat-file --batch-check receives only deduplicated selected blob OIDs.
The added metadata calls do not authorize an enlarged file set.

Every native command retains exclusive ATTEMPT and input/raw stream files
created before spawn, actual PID and requested new-session group ownership,
full exact environment, actual exit/timeout/exception and bounded handling.
The source does not label its derived signal-group identifier as an observed
proc-group sample. stdout/stderr are owned pipes; communicate must observe
their EOF as well as native exit zero before a successful command result.
Actual bytes are saved into preopened raw files. Timeout partial bytes are
preserved separately and are not relabelled complete originals.

The accepted private-checkpoint policy is a 50-second command bound, TERM
with at most 5 seconds waiting and then KILL with at most 3 seconds waiting
for the still-owned leader/group; a final pipe drain is bounded at 3 seconds.
Cancellation is separately recorded. If the leader is already reaped while
another writer keeps a pipe open, no unsupported new group ownership is
invented: missing EOF remains UNKNOWN. There is no retry or alternate command.
This is the accepted private-Git timeout mechanism, deliberately not P212's
different no-automatic-intervention outer policy. It is not an exhaustive
process-tree or escaped-process proof. Root must receive actual native and
outer closure, not infer it from a wrapper exit.

The executor DOES NOT produce a final phase manifest. It returns
NATIVE_PHASE_COMPLETE_ROOT_PRODUCT_PENDING, with phase_seal null, after
internal checks. Root must then attach the actual enclosing tool request,
initial result and every actual yield/session/poll/final return, including
any unknowns or failures, to the same phase capture using a finite exclusive
attachment. A thrown tool error is not an invented native exit. No replay is
needed solely to attach values that already exist.

After independently reading the complete source/plan/input/native/product
originals, root writes ROOT_RECEPTION.json with this exact schema:

    schema: checkpoint03-phase-root-reception-v1
    status: ROOT_ACCEPTED_PRIVATE_CHECKPOINT_PHASE
    phase: the actual completed phase
    run: the actual unique run path
    scope_sha256: the fixed chosen scope hash
    source_sha256: the actual received executor hash
    result_sha256: the actual complete RESULT.json hash
    actual_outer_product_closed: true
    complete_native_streams_received: true
    previous_phase: the exact prior seal pin or null for capture

The receipt contains no own manifest hash. Root then creates the complete
nonself MANIFEST.sha256 over all phase files, including product originals and
that receipt, after they exist. A new successor binding pins both the actual
manifest and root receipt. The executor checks the complete previous chain,
not merely the most recent native result. Root decisions remain independent;
this schema is not author/root acceptance or permission to forge true fields.

## Four operations, no automatic successor

Capture rechecks actual BASE/remote/roles, the exact 182 membership groups,
all selected file keys and current capacity before Git mutation could occur.
Capacity must be at least 2,333,581,815 bytes on both /root and the accepted
bare filesystem; payload ceiling is 400,000,000 bytes. The source uses an
actual tempfile.mkdtemp-owned /root/symbolic-dynamics-checkpoint03-* run, prints
its real path immediately and creates a distinct initially empty isolated
index parent. No cache/workspace/existing run is deleted or overwritten.
Only selected files are copied, with raw source/copy/after equality and
identity checks. The exact chosen/core/bridge plans and executor are saved
as local run metadata, not added to the Git selection. Capture creates no
index/object/ref. It stops for root product reception.

Stage starts with the actual accepted capture and still absent isolated
index. Only read-tree BASE, selected hash-object --no-filters --stdin-paths,
exact NUL-delimited update-index --index-info and write-tree are allowed.
Returned OIDs must equal independently computed frozen blob OIDs; native
LF/TAB/NUL framing is literal. Complete selected index/tree/object metadata
and the whole unfiltered baseline diff must match. No default-index write,
deletion or nonselected tree modification is allowed. The actual isolated
index key is recorded for later phases. Stage stops before any commit.

Commit rechecks the accepted stage, unchanged whole frozen payload/index,
BASE/remote/roles and actual tree/diff. The sole mutation is one commit-tree
with exactly BASE as parent and the existing command-local identity. The
complete returned commit bytes are independently hashed; exactly four
expected headers and the fixed narrow message are required. Main must remain
BASE. This unreferenced commit object is not a private synchronization.
Commit stops before any push.

Push rechecks the accepted commit and full preceding chain, immutable
tree/parent/diff/frozen index, protected roles and actual remote BASE. It
performs one ordinary non-force push to the explicit private URL, confirms
actual remote COMMIT, then compare-and-swap updates bare main from BASE.
Further actual local/remote/tree/parent/mirror checks follow. If a push succeeds
but CAS or later reception fails, the partial remote state remains preserved
and must be reported as such: no rollback, retry, force or invented success.

All size and deadline values are proposed guards, not measured timing,
reserved storage or a future successful run. No current group membership,
capacity, Git/SSH role or remote state was checked in this source-only task.
